LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING ) 15.1.1 ORAL AND SIGNED REPORTS- NEWS (ROLE PLAY)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.1: Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking ) 15.1.1 Oral and signed Reports- News (role play)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking ) 15.1.1 Oral and signed Reports- News (role play), part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why are oral or signed reports important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking ) 15.1.1 Oral and signed Reports- News (role play) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: interacting with technology as they watch and listen to or observe signed audio visual recordings of News

and signed reports.

• Communication and collaboration: teamwork as learners work in pairs and groups to record signed reports.

Values:
• Respect: learners listen to or observe signed reports and critique others as they orally or through signing present reports.

• Love: learners listen to or observe signed reports and record other speeches and give necessary support and provide

constructive feedback.

185

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Learners support program- Effective communication: learners present news reports through sign language with confidence.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: Why are oral or signed reports important?
